chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Sufyan ibn Khalid, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, that he was praying one day when a man passed in front of him while his son Musa was sitting there. When he finished, he said:
to him: “O my father, did you not see the man who passed in front of you?” So he said: “O my son, the One for whom I pray is nearer to me than the one who passed in front of me.”
So the correct understanding of this report is permissibility, while the merit is in what we have previously presented among the reports, and this further clarifies that.

key_terms.أَقْرَبُ إِلَيَّ: nearer to me; expressing spiritual attentiveness and nearness
key_terms.أُصَلِّي لَهُ: the One for whom I perform salat (prayer), meaning Allah
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: what is more virtuous or preferable
key_terms.يَا بُنَيَّ: O my son; an affectionate form of address to one’s child

ai.seo_question: Does someone passing in front of a person during salat (prayer) affect the validity of the prayer?
ai.summary: This report describes that a man passed in front of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام while he was in salat (prayer), and the Imam did not turn his attention to him because of his focus on Allah. The concluding note explains that such passing does not invalidate the prayer, though earlier reports indicate a more excellent etiquette regarding the space before the worshipper.
